title: Simple Deployment
summary: Moving a Dockerized full-stack app from your laptop to a real AWS EC2 server: how IP addresses and DNS route traffic, launching an Ubuntu instance with a key pair and security group, connecting over SSH, installing Docker, then `docker compose up -d` and running migrations on the live server. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Deploy a Dockerized full-stack app to an AWS EC2 instance and open it from any browser.

steps.title: Get an AWS account ready safely
steps.detail: The lesson secures the root user with MFA, creates an IAM admin user for daily work, and sets billing alerts. Before signing up or entering a card, confirm in #eagle_questions whether the course provides AWS accounts or credits.
steps.doneWhen: You know which AWS account you'll use, and (if it's yours) MFA is on and a billing alert exists.

steps.title: Check SSH on your Mac
steps.detail: SSH is how you'll control the server from your terminal. AWS gives you a .pem key file, and SSH refuses to use it unless only you can read it.
steps.doneWhen: `ssh -V` prints a version, and you can explain why `chmod 600 key.pem` is needed.

steps.title: Have a Compose app running locally
steps.detail: Deploying is repeating what works locally on a remote machine. Your FS 1 / FS 2 app should start with one command.
steps.doneWhen: `docker compose up -d` then `docker compose ps` shows every service as running on your Mac.
